facts.text: Aida was commissioned by Cairo’s Khedivial Opera House and premiered there on 24 December 1871.
facts.evidence: it was commissioned by Cairo's Khedivial Opera House and had its première there on 24 December 1871

facts.text: The premiere was delayed because the sets and costumes were stuck in Paris during the Prussian siege of 1870–71.
facts.evidence: Because the scenery and costumes were stuck in the French capital during the Siege of Paris (1870–71)

facts.text: Verdi didn’t go to Cairo. He disliked that the audience was all invited dignitaries and critics, and counted the 1872 La Scala opening as the real premiere.
evidence: Although Verdi did not attend the premiere in Cairo
He therefore considered the Italian (and European) première, held at La Scala, Milan on 8 February 1872

facts.text: Verdi wrote a full overture to replace this short prelude, then dropped it for its “pretentious silliness” (his own words).
evidence: He then composed an overture of the "potpourri" variety to replace the original prelude.

facts.text: Verdi’s rejected Aida overture got a rare broadcast in 1940 from Toscanini and the NBC Symphony, but was never released commercially.
facts.evidence: was given a rare broadcast performance by Arturo Toscanini and the NBC Symphony Orchestra on 30 March 1940, but was never commercially issued

facts.text: Verdi agreed to write Aida, on a story idea by the Egyptologist Auguste Mariette, for 150,000 francs.
facts.evidence: Verdi agreed to compose an opera based on that story, for 150,000 francs

facts.text: Auguste Mariette designed the costumes for the Cairo premiere; the sets were painted in Paris by the Opéra’s scene painters.
facts.evidence: The costumes and accessories for the première were designed by Auguste Mariette

facts.text: Verdi wrote the role of Aida for Teresa Stolz, who first sang it at the Milan premiere.
facts.evidence: Verdi had also written the role of Aida for the voice of Teresa Stolz

facts.sceneMatch: Amneris|Fu la sorte|Ohimè! morir mi sento|L.abborrita rivale
facts.text: Maria Waldmann, the Milan Amneris, was Verdi’s favourite in the role; she sang it many times at his request.
facts.evidence: The Milan Amneris, Maria Waldmann, was his favourite in the role and she repeated it a number of times at his request.

facts.text: In Rio de Janeiro in 1886, after the conductor and two replacements failed, a 19-year-old cellist named Arturo Toscanini conducted Aida from memory, with great success.
evidence: Arturo Toscanini, at the time a 19-year-old cellist who was assistant chorus master, was persuaded to conduct the performance.
He conducted the opera from memory with great success.

facts.text: At the Met alone, Aida has been sung more than 1,100 times since 1886.
facts.evidence: At New York's Metropolitan Opera alone, Aida has been sung more than 1,100 times since 1886.

facts.text: Aida reached the Met on 12 November 1886, conducted by Anton Seidl.
facts.evidence: Metropolitan Opera, New York: 12 November 1886, conducted by Anton Seidl

facts.text: The King names Radamès commander, and the court erupts: “Su! del Nilo al sacro lido”, then “Guerra, guerra, guerra!”
facts.evidence: "Su! del Nilo al sacro lido" .. (reprise) "Guerra, guerra, guerra!"
